text:
Ben (infra): Heads-up — our March invoice has a new line labeled 'Accelerator forwarding fee' for several us-west1 GPU instances. Didn’t see this last month. Anyone know what that is? :thinking:
Aisha (finops): I’m seeing the same. Appears on both on-demand and reserved pools. Amounts look tiny per-hour but total is ~5% of the GPU spend for the month.
Marcus (cloudops): Hmm — forwarding fee? Could be related to some cross-subnet / egress routing change. Did we change VPC peering or NAT config in late Feb?
Lina (eng): We did flip a new NLB in front of the inference pool on Feb 27 for Canary. Might be touching traffic path.
Ben (infra): I pulled the invoice CSV. Here are the relevant lines:
```
InvoiceID,SKU,Region,ResourceDescription,UsageHours,Amount
INV-2026-03,Accelerator forwarding fee,us-west1,accelerator-12345,720,48.60
INV-2026-03,Accelerator forwarding fee,us-east4,accelerator-67890,480,32.40
INV-2026-03,GPU compute (on-demand),us-west1,n1-accelerator,720,1120.00
```
Aisha (finops): That SKU isn't in our price book. I searched commit/discount mappings and nothing references 'forwarding fee'. I’m opening a ticket with the provider. billing-bot: Created support ticket CLOUD-BILL-1123 and attached invoice extract.
Marcus (cloudops): I can correlate billing tags to instances. If the fee is per-accelerator hour that originates from cross-zone forwarding, it might be charged when the NVLink traffic crosses a fabric boundary. But that's unusual for user-level workloads.
Lina (eng): Canary NLB we added routes some inference shards through gateway-hosts in another AZ for balancing. Could those gateways be triggering a data-path that the cloud bills as 'forwarding'?
Aisha (finops): Provider replied: "Accelerator forwarding fee applies when accelerator-attached traffic is routed through managed firewalls or third-party virtual appliances that cause traffic hairpin." They asked for example resource IDs.
Ben (infra): Marcus — can you run a flowtrace on the inference pool from last week? Need sample resource IDs to challenge the charge.
Marcus (cloudops): On it. Quick check shows three instances with NIC path through the NVA cluster: accel-12345, accel-12346, accel-12347. Sending logs + netflow snippet to this thread.
Ben (infra): Thanks. Netflow excerpt:
```
2026-03-05T13:12:02Z accel-12345 -> nva-01 : internal-forward 10.0.3.12:1234 -> 10.1.8.4:5678
2026-03-05T13:12:02Z accel-12346 -> nva-02 : internal-forward 10.0.3.13:1234 -> 10.1.8.5:5678
```
Aisha (finops): Good. I replied to CLOUD-BILL-1123 with the resource IDs and netflow. Asked them to either credit the forwarding fee or confirm it's legitimately billable due to our NVA configuration.
billing-bot: CLOUD-BILL-1123 updated: Provider ack'd receipt, estimated 48–72h for investigation.
Lina (eng): Short-term mitigation: can we disable the NLB cross-AZ balancing for the inference canary? Might route traffic without hairpin. If that reduces forwarding events, we can avoid charge while provider investigates.
Marcus (cloudops): We can toggle stickiness and zone-local routing tonight during low traffic window. ETA 22:00 PT.
Ben (infra): Please add a dashboard alert to detect 'Accelerator forwarding fee' spikes and tag future instances that touch the NVA so finops can filter reports.
Aisha (finops): Will do. Also proposing we add a pre-deploy billing checklist: any NVA or third-party virtual appliance change must be approved by FinOps for potential forwarding charges.
Lina (eng): Makes sense. Can we get a rollback plan if disabling cross-AZ routing impacts latency/throughput?
Marcus (cloudops): I'll draft a canary rollback script and run load tests after routing change.
Aisha (finops): Closing loop: if provider credits the fee, we'll apply as invoice adjustment and update the month-end report. If not, we need to model recurring forwarding cost into our reserved capacity projections.
Ben (infra): Thanks team — keep updates in the ticket and drop a short note here after the 22:00 change. :thumbsup:
